Resolves #21097

A mouse event's data now carries the `pointerType` that produced it. `Neo.main.DomEvents#getMouseEventData` copies the field with the others: `'mouse'`, `'pen'` or `'touch'` from a `PointerEvent` (a click in current Chromium), and `undefined` from a `MouseEvent` (a dblclick, a mousedown, or a click in a browser that dispatches one). The JSDoc says how to read the gap: `undefined` means no signal, so a consumer falls back to the device, never to "mouse".

The first consumer is the web desktop launcher in #21087 (#21075), which carries this commit. A tap opens an app, while a mouse click on the same touch-capable computer only selects; Emmy's review of #21087 asked for that.

Evidence: L1 (unit) → L1 required (the change is a serialized field; its consumer's browser behavior is witnessed in #21087). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 a click carrying `pointerType` reaches the app with it | CI: `test/playwright/unit/main/DomEvents.spec.mjs` "a click reaches the app with the pointer type that produced it; a mouse event without one sends undefined": clicks with `'touch'` and `'mouse'` reach `sendMessageToApp` with those values. |
| AC-2 an event without one sends `undefined`; the other fields are unchanged | Same arm: the dblclick sends `pointerType: undefined`, and the click keeps `button`, `clientX`, `clientY` and `type`. |
| AC-3 the JSDoc names the field and its fallback | `getMouseEventData`'s JSDoc. |
